arch.aside.1.b: endpoints / transport / scheme / timeout / retry / auth; falls back to ETCD_* environment variables.
arch.aside.2.b: EtcdClient::instance() for no-DI setups such as Webman; resetInstance() for tests.
arch.aside.3.b: only transport-level failures retry, up to retry times, 100ms×n linear backoff, endpoint rotated.
arch.aside.4.b: the gRPC-gateway wants key / value as base64 strings; both directions convert automatically.
arch.aside.5.b: prefixToRangeEnd() increments the last byte for the upper bound; all-0xFF falls back to \x00.
arch.aside.title: Cross-cutting concerns
arch.dep.title: Runtime dependencies
arch.exc.title: Exception tree — all extend RuntimeException, split by retryable semantics
arch.facade: EtcdClient — single entry point, lazily builds the six subsystems
arch.http.sub1: etcd's built-in gRPC-gateway, JSON over HTTP
arch.msg.body: Plain PHP data classes, not extending Google\Protobuf\Internal\Message; the transport encodes with them, they are not a network hop.
arch.msg.title: Message layer · protobuf stubs
arch.sel.body: transport = auto / http / grpc; auto currently means http (gRPC covers unary RPCs only; streaming and Election still need HTTP), only an explicit grpc selects it
arch.watch.sub: watch / watchPrefix · resumes after a drop
common.arch_desc: Five layers: framework adapters, facade, subsystem clients, transport and the etcd server, plus cross-cutting concerns, the message layer and the exception tree.
common.arch_sub: PHP etcd v3 client — layers, dependency direction and error semantics
common.feat_desc: KV, Watch, Lease, Auth, Cluster and Maintenance, with their methods and behavioural contracts.
common.feat_sub: Six API domains — methods and behavioural contracts
common.life_desc: The request, watch and lease lifecycles.
common.life_sub: One request, one watch, one lease — three tracks
feat.auth.n: Permission types 0=READ 1=WRITE 2=READWRITE; once auth is on, the client needs auth.user / auth.password.
feat.cluster.n: A learner joins without a vote, then gets promoted to voter, so scaling out never breaks quorum.
feat.cluster.s: member add/remove and the learner lifecycle
feat.footer: Every failure raises a typed exception from Erikwang2013\Etcd\Exception; the HTTP and gRPC transports share one subsystem API.
feat.kv.n: Results come back as associative arrays; getOrFail() raises KeyNotFoundException; txn uses the compare → success / failure form.
feat.kv.s: core reads and writes, prefix scans, atomic transactions
feat.lease.n: Service registration: grant + put(lease) + a periodic keepAlive heartbeat; a crashed process needs no cleanup.
feat.lease.s: keys with a TTL, cleaned up by etcd on expiry
feat.maint.n: snapshot() returns raw binary through sendRaw(), ready to be written to disk as a backup.
feat.watch.n: After EOF it backs off 100ms×n and reconnects to another endpoint, so failover loses no events.
feat.watch.s: long-lived event stream over HTTP chunked
life.r1.a.2: merges defaults, reads ETCD_* env vars
life.r1.b.2: key and value go through base64_encode
life.r1.c.1: random endpoint, PSR-18 client posts to /v3/*
life.r1.c.2: transport failure: retry up to retry times
life.r1.note: Failure branch: only ConnectionException retries; auth and server errors are thrown straight to the caller.
life.r1.s: synchronous calls: from construction to error semantics
life.r2.b.3: split the buffer into JSON frames by line
life.r2.c.1: decode PUT / DELETE events and header.revision
life.r2.c.2: remember lastRevision as the resume anchor
life.r2.c.3: hand the events to your callback
life.r2.d.1: EOF or a dropped socket → backoff, new endpoint
life.r2.note: Loop: ④ falls back to ② to rebuild the connection; lastRevision makes it resume where it stopped.
life.r3.a.2: returns {ID, TTL}; an ID may be reused
life.r3.a.3: the TTL is timed by the etcd server
life.r3.b.2: one lease can bind many keys
life.r3.b.3: keys live and die with the lease
life.r3.c.1: a timer calls keepAlive($ID) to refresh the TTL
life.r3.c.3: a successful renew means the service is alive
life.r3.d.1: the TTL reaches zero, or revoke() is called
life.r3.d.3: a crashed process needs no cleanup
life.r3.note: Loop: ③ repeats every TTL/3 until the service goes away — a distributed health check.
life.r3.s: service registration: TTL heartbeat and cleanup
